# Plan: Actionable "Mark today complete" empty state for Habit Strength

## Context

On the Habit Detail screen, the **Habit Strength** card currently shows a passive
empty state when a habit has zero completions: a dashed box reading *"Not enough
data yet / Complete your first day to start building strength."* It's a dead end —
nothing to do, no path forward.

The attached mock (`.context/attachments/vCp4SQ/image.png`) proposes turning that
empty state into a **3-step path to the first milestone** with a primary
**"Mark today complete"** button. Tapping it completes today's habit, which then
flips the card from empty → the live strength view (ring + chart + stats).

Decisions confirmed with the user:

1. **The button performs the real completion toggle** (reusing the existing
   handler), and the card transitions to the live view afterward.
2. **Keep the mock's layout, but use the app's real first-milestone language** —
   not the mock's invented "SEED · TIER 0 / Seed / first tier" vocabulary. The
   real first milestone is **"Habit Starter" at a 3-day streak** (`MILESTONES[0]`,
   badge ⚡), and the first strength level is **"Starting"**.

## How the data flows (verified)

- `HabitStrengthSection` (`src/components/HabitStrengthSection/HabitStrengthSection.tsx:60`)
  renders `<StrengthEmptyState>` when `isEmpty` (i.e. `completedDates.size === 0`,
  per `HabitStrengthSection.hooks.ts:93`). It already receives `habitId` but never
  uses it.
- Parent `HabitDetailContent.tsx:81` renders the section and already has
  `onDayPress: (dateString, isCompleted) => void`, wired up the chain to
  `handleCalendarDayPress` (`useCalendarHandlers.ts:54`) — the real toggle, with a
  rate-limit guard, future-date rejection (today is allowed), optimistic update,
  haptics, and error handling.
- So the button handler is simply `onDayPress(getLocalDateString(), false)`
  (`getLocalDateString` at `src/utils/getLocalDateString.ts:25`; `false` =
  "not yet completed"). After the toggle, `completedDates` becomes size 1,
  `isEmpty` flips false, and the section re-renders as the live view — no extra
  transition logic needed.

## Implementation

### 1. Thread a completion callback into the section
- **`src/components/HabitStrengthSection/types.ts`** — add to
  `HabitStrengthSectionProps`: `onMarkTodayComplete?: () => void`.
- **`HabitStrengthSection.tsx`** — accept `onMarkTodayComplete` and pass it to
  `<StrengthEmptyState>`. (No other branch uses it.)
- **`HabitDetailContent.tsx`** — pass
  `onMarkTodayComplete={() => onDayPress(getLocalDateString(), false)}` to
  `<HabitStrengthSection>` (import `getLocalDateString`). `onDayPress` is already a
  prop here, so nothing changes above this file.

### 2. Rewrite `StrengthEmptyState.tsx` to match the mock (with real language)
Keep the outer card + "Habit Strength" title. Replace the inner content:

- **Title row:** `Habit Strength` (left) + a small pill badge (right) showing the
  starting level — `{startingEmoji} Starting` using `colors.strength.startingLight`
  background / `colors.strength.starting` text (import from `@/theme/colors`).
- **Inner panel** (keep the dashed border for the "empty" feel):
  - Starting emoji in the rounded circle (unchanged).
  - **Heading:** `3 days to Habit Starter` (source from `MILESTONES[0]` in
    `src/components/ProgressSectionConsolidated/milestones.data.ts` — reuse
    `.days`, `.name`, `.badge`; do not hardcode).
  - **Body:** `Strength grows the more days you show up. Miss a day? Your streak
    shield protects you. Complete today to start.` (Kept the shield line per the
    user; reworded to "streak shield" since a real streak-freeze/rescue mechanic
    exists — `src/utils/notifications/streakFreeze.ts` — and it protects the
    streak, not the momentum strength.)
  - **Path dots:** a row of `MILESTONES[0].days` (3) small dots, all unfilled,
    with caption `Day 0 of 3 · Starting`. Minor wording flexibility allowed.
  - **Primary button:** "Mark today complete" — dark pill
    (`backgroundColor: themeColors.text.primary`, label color `themeColors.card`,
    height 44 / `componentSpacing.button`, `borderRadius.button`). Calls
    `onMarkTodayComplete`. Must have `accessibilityRole="button"` and
    `accessibilityLabel="Mark today complete"`. **Reuse an existing button
    primitive if one exists** (check `src/components/` for a shared Button before
    writing a raw `Pressable`).

Match existing token usage: `typography` (heading3/body/caption), `spacing`,
`borderRadius`, `shadows` from `src/theme/*`, and `useThemeColors()`.

### 3. Respect the 100-line rule (project CLAUDE.md)
The richer layout will push `StrengthEmptyState.tsx` over 100 non-comment lines.
Decompose as needed — e.g. extract a `MarkTodayCompleteButton.tsx` and/or a small
`MilestonePathDots.tsx` co-located in the `HabitStrengthSection/` folder — so each
file stays ≤100 lines. Verify with `npm run lint:max-lines`.

## Notes / guardrails
- The button only ever appears at zero completions, so `isCompletedToday` is
  always false in this state — no need to handle an "already completed" label.
- Don't add a new mutation or hook; reuse `onDayPress` end-to-end.
- Use **npm** for this project (project CLAUDE.md), not bun.
- The mock's secondary ideas (forecast curve, density strip, sparklines, streak
  shield card, growth ladder, heatmap variants) are **out of scope** — this change
  is only the empty-state card.

## Verification
1. `npx tsc --noEmit` (or project typecheck script) — no type errors.
2. `npm run lint:max-lines` — no new violations from the changed/added files.
3. Unit test: add/update a test for `StrengthEmptyState` asserting the button
   calls `onMarkTodayComplete` when pressed (check for an existing
   `HabitStrengthSection` `__tests__` dir first; follow its patterns).
4. Run the app (`npm run ios` / Expo) → open a **brand-new habit with zero
   completions** → Habit Detail → Strength card shows the new empty state →
   tap **"Mark today complete"** → confirm: today toggles complete (haptic +
   optimistic check), and the card transitions to the live ring/chart/stats view.
   Also verify the previously-completed case is unaffected (open a habit with
   history → live view renders as before).

allowedPrompts.prompt: run typecheck, lint, and unit tests (npm run *, npx tsc)
run the app via expo/npm to verify the empty state
